lead_headline: PHO & WOK opens in College View while Port Side closes after a decade in Five Points

restaurant.blurb: 4 leads today: PHO & WOK opened in College View (January), Borama Mexican Brunch in Westminster, Cafe Crêpes at Junction Food & Drink. One closure: Port Side after 10 years.

liquor.blurb: The blackout enters Week 7. Zero new applications detected today — Saturday marks day 44 of the freeze that began June 1. The 7-day window shows 274 applications, but that figure remains a stale artifact of backdated batch corrections, not live filings. No genuine new activity since May 31. Weekend typically sees zero filings, so today's silence carries no diagnostic weight — but the pattern persists: 12,512 tracked licenses, completely dormant application pipeline, six consecutive weeks without state explanation. Monday will mark 46 business days frozen. The capital markets theory strengthens as July provides no seasonal resumption. Either hospitality investment collapsed statewide in lockstep, or Colorado's licensing apparatus stopped functioning without public notice. Both scenarios point to structural failure, not administrative delay.

Week closes 74 mentions across 15 sources, down marginally from last week's 76 (−3%) but holding steady post-holiday baseline. Denver Post leads weekly (19 citations), followed by Instagram (15), Facebook (14), Reddit (11). Google News RSS captured 73 of 74 (99% efficiency). The week's pattern: consistent mid-70s range for third consecutive week, stable sourcing diversity at 15 outlets. Friday's 4-mention day matches typical weekend drop-off, not momentum shift.

subscriptions.blurb: Net −1 yesterday (0 new, 1 canceled) — ninth straight zero-or-negative day pushes July's crisis into uncharted territory. MTD holds at +2 (+0.2/day), 90-day net slips to +113. The deterioration accelerates: after June's explosive close (+17 net June 29-30), July opened modestly (+10 first three days), then flatlined completely. July 4-11: nine consecutive days without positive net, the longest acquisition drought on record. The +0.2/day MTD pace lags YTD baseline by 83% (vs +1.2/day historical). Week 2 closes worse than Week 1: 7-day window shows −7 net (23 new, 30 canceled), sustained negative momentum unseen since May. Churn accelerates while new subscriptions vanish — 30 cancellations in 7 days vs 21 the prior week, 43% increase. Remove June 30's carryover and July runs definitively negative through eleven days. No gain above +1 since July 3. The YTD +1.2/day average now represents historical performance only — current reality runs 90% below trend with no recovery signal emerging.
